description: Every note type in the Story Forge vault. The sf tool validates against this file, the app renders boards and forms from it, and Templates/ is generated from it. Change a type here and nowhere else.

conventions.links: Obsidian wiki links in quotes, "[[Name]]". The name must match the target note's title or name exactly.

scopes.vault: folder is relative to the vault root
scopes.book: folder is relative to Series/<Series>/Books/<N Title>/

conventions.enum: either the name of a status set below, or a literal list of values
conventions.computed: filled by the tool, never by hand
conventions.extraProperties: a type with extraProperties true accepts properties it does not list (System/Config.md uses this for its settings)
conventions.extends: a note with an extends property is a book delta of a series note and holds only what differs
conventions.secrets: twists and hidden facts go in a > [!secret] callout in the body; packets withhold them unless a scene's reveal list names the note. A callout titled with a scene (> [!secret] Book 1, S-039) is revealed by that scene and known in every packet after it
conventions.first_seen: where a bible note first appears on the page, as Book 1, S-005; packets for earlier scenes leave the note out
conventions.later: an inbox idea tagged later is one Kyle put aside on the Ideas board to come back to; its status stays inbox. Keep and drop on the board set status keep or discard, the decided time and any reason in decision_note; nothing is moved or deleted
conventions.accepted: Kyle accepts a scene card on the Chapter Grid; the app sets accepted to the time he tapped. Needs work removes accepted and puts his reason in decision_note. Beats and conflicts are kept or dropped on their boards the way ideas are, and market notes (market case, comps, keyword sets, titles) on the Market board
conventions.scene_title: A scene card's title is a one-line summary of what happens in the scene (Kyle, 2026-10-17, T-009), such as "Grey turns down the guild's offer". Agents write titles that way and read them as the scene's summary. The file name follows the title (S-012 <title>.md); Kyle changes it from Edit card in the app, which renames the file.
conventions.regenerate: Rewrite on a board sets a proposal's status to regenerate, the decided time, and what Kyle wants changed in decision_note. The agent that owns the note rewrites it from that note and sets it back to inbox
conventions.headline: a scene's headline is one sentence saying what happens, shown as its header in the app. The team writes it from the prose when it is empty (System/Tools/jobs.mjs makes a summaries job); Kyle may change it, and the team never rewrites a headline that is filled in

common.description: Properties every type accepts. created and updated are dates; updated is computed.

series.description: A series. Every book lives inside one, even a series of one.
series.body: What the series is about, the series-level story question, and notes that hold across books.

book.description: One book. Its shape (length, chapters, framework) is a setting here, never a design constant.
book.body: Pitch, synopsis and working notes for the book.

book-spec.description: The single input to one-shot mode. Status inbox until Kyle keeps it.
book-spec.body: Anything the one-shot run must know that the properties do not hold.

market-thesis.description: A niche drilldown ending in a one-paragraph thesis.
market-thesis.body: The thesis paragraph, then the evidence from the exports with file names and dates.

comp.description: A comparable title doing the exact thing. A comp is proof, not inspiration.
comp.body: Notes on what the comp proves and where each number came from.

keyword-set.description: Seven KDP keywords, three categories and the promises the book must deliver.
keyword-set.body: Where each keyword came from (the search terms and export).

title-candidate.description: A title, subtitle and series name, tested against the comps.
title-candidate.body: Why the title signals the niche, and how it reads next to each comp.

cover-brief.description: The brief for the cover artist. Covers are per book.
cover-brief.body: The brief as sent, must-haves, must-avoids, and a dated feedback log of every round of notes.

cover-comps.description: The comp cover board for the artist.
cover-comps.body: One section per comp cover, with the image embedded from Cover/Comps/.

cover-iteration.description: One round of art from the cover artist.

idea.description: Any proposal: premise, Big Issue, opinion, twist, editorial note. Kyle keeps, regenerates or discards.

reasons.description: One-press reasons Kyle gave with Keep, Later or Drop. They teach the team his taste.

round.description: The brainstorm round the idea came from (1 blind pitch, 2 response, 3 fusion), so the keep rate per round shows if later rounds earn their cost.

idea.body: Three sections: ## The idea, ## Why it could work, ## Risks / costs.

character.description: Series canon for a character. A book delta (with extends) holds only what differs in one book.

arc_points.description: The character's arc scene by scene, as "S-012: 4": 0 is fully in the Lie, 10 fully living the Truth (Character Arcs).

arc_draft.description: True while arc_points are the team's guess and Kyle has not changed or confirmed them.

character.body: Who they are, how they sound, relationships in detail. Secrets go in a > [!secret] callout.

place.description: A place in the series world.
place.body: Description and history. Secrets go in a > [!secret] callout.

lore.description: A rule, system or piece of history in the series world.
lore.body: The full rule and its consequences. Secrets go in a > [!secret] callout.

item.description: Gear, artefacts, loot: what people carry and trade.
item.body: Description, stats, history. Secrets go in a > [!secret] callout.

thread.description: A plot thread with its own dramatic question.
thread.body: How the thread runs across the book or series. Secrets go in a > [!secret] callout.

progression.description: A state change at a point in the manuscript. Replaces hand-kept state in Story So Far.

beat.description: A structural beat in the book's framework, with the scenes that deliver it.
beat.body: What happens in the beat and why it sits here.

conflict.description: A collision from one of the three conflict sources, run for three cause-and-effect beats.
conflict.body: The collision in full, beat by beat.

scene.description: A scene card in the properties and the prose in the body.

threads.description: Story threads this scene moves (Plot Grid).

day.description: Story day the scene happens on, counting from day 1 (Timeline).

tension.description: How tense the scene is, 1 to 10 (Tension and Pacing).

outcome.description: How the point-of-view character's goal turns out: yes, yes-but, no, no-and.

mood.description: How the scene feels, from -5 (dark) to 5 (bright) (story shape).

card_draft.description: Card fields the team filled in that Kyle has not confirmed yet (the app shows them as the team's guess until he changes or confirms them).

scene.body: The prose, or for a planned scene the card notes.

promise.description: A setup the reader is owed a payoff for.
promise.body: What was promised and how it will pay off.

theme.body: How the theme is dramatised, never stated.

previously.description: What a finished book changed in the series. The next book's agents read every one.
previously.body: What changed in series canon, open threads at the end, and the cast state table.

session.description: The record of one substantial thread: who took part, what was decided.
session.body: One ## Round heading per round, voices as > [!voice] callouts, then ## Kyle's decisions and ## Reflection.

note.description: A standing instruction from Kyle to the team. Agents handle open notes first.

recipe.description: A standing instruction of Kyle's in plain English, used by name ("draft chapter 4 with the cliffhanger recipe"). Any agent that is handed a recipe follows it on top of its usual rules.

use_for.description: What it is for, in a few words (a chapter end, a stat block).

decision.description: One decision about a book, with who made it and why. Studio-wide decisions go in the Decision Ledger instead.
decision.body: The decision, the options weighed, and what would change it.

research.body: The findings, each tied to a source in the list or marked unverified.

task.description: A piece of work with an owner. Studio and system to-dos live in the vault's Tasks/ (the nightly validate files its problems there). A book's to-dos live in that book's Tasks/ and are about its pages: `chapter` (and `scene`) say where, and `generated: true` marks one the team found in a check rather than one Kyle wrote. The writing screen shows a chapter's to-dos beside the page.

chapter.description: Book to-dos: the chapter it is about.

scene.description: Book to-dos: the scene it is about, when it is about one.

generated.description: True when the team wrote it after a check; Kyle's own to-dos leave it out.

found_by.description: For a generated to-do: the check that found it (continuity, plot, character, line, genre).

done_note.description: When the team marks a to-do done: one line on what in the text fixed it, so Kyle can reopen it if he disagrees.

task.body: What needs doing and how to tell it is done.

writing-day.description: Kyle's Pomodoros on one day, written by the app's timer: how many he finished, the minutes and the words written during them. Lives in Writing Log/ at the vault root, one note per day.

minutes.description: Minutes of work Pomodoros, including ones stopped early.

words.description: Words written during them, stopped ones included, after deletions (can be below zero on a cutting day).

writing-day.body: ## Pomodoros: one line per Pomodoro, `- HH:MM, N minutes, W words (S-012, S-013)`, with `(stopped early)` after the minutes for one stopped before its time (it adds minutes and words, not to pomodoros), oldest first. The app appends lines and never rewrites earlier ones.

style-guide.description: The book's voice rules. Overrides the default prose rules.
style-guide.body: The voice in plain words, with short approved examples.

story-so-far.description: The rolling summary the Writer reads before drafting.
story-so-far.body: What has happened so far, chapter by chapter.

braindump.description: Anything Kyle wants the team to know, in any order.
braindump.body: Free text from Kyle. Agents read it; they never edit it.

scene-notes.description: A scene's planning notes, kept beside its prose so the writing screen shows only the story: Kyle's outline, the team's notes and questions, and where the scene came from. One note per scene; the writing screen shows it under the scene's card.

scene.description: The scene these notes are about.

title.description: The scene's title, so the file is easy to find.

scene-notes.body: Callouts as they stood in the scene: Kyle's outline, Team notes (bible proposals and continuity questions), Open for Kyle questions and Source lines. Agents add new team notes here, not in the prose.

chapter-beats.description: A chapter's beats: the moves of the chapter, each a short title and a one-line summary, kept beside the prose so the scenes hold only the story. The app shows the chapter by its beats, each opening to its prose, and Kyle edits beats and prose there.

chapter.description: The chapter these beats belong to.

chapter-beats.body: One `## ` heading per beat, in reading order: the beat's title. Under it, the one-line summary, then `Starts: S-NNN · <first words>`: the scene the beat sits in and the first ten words of the paragraph it starts at, copied exactly without * or = marks. A beat with no prose yet has `Starts: S-NNN` and no words. Never put beats in the scene files. See `.claude/skills/chapter-beats/SKILL.md`.

chapter-plan.description: Kyle's plan for a chapter, as many paragraphs as he likes, kept beside the prose so the scenes hold only the story. The writing screen shows it in the right-hand column (the Plan tab) and Kyle writes it there.

chapter.description: The chapter this plan is for.

chapter-plan.body: Kyle's words, free text. Agents read it whenever they work on the chapter (sf packet includes it) and never edit it.

knowledge.description: A craft note in the Library. Shelves are subfolders.
knowledge.body: The craft knowledge, with the framework or source named.

persona.description: A reader persona the Beta Reader reads as.
persona.body: Who this reader is, what they love, what makes them stop reading, how they report.

system-doc.description: Documentation and system notes: Docs/, System/, Taste/.

job.description: A request for an agent to do one piece of work, made from the app or a thread. GitHub runs requested jobs (.github/workflows/agent-jobs.yml) and the runner updates the note as it goes. Lives in Jobs/ at the vault root.
job.body: ## Ask holds Kyle's words. The runner appends ## Result. For kind chat, thread names the conversation (a scene ID or chat-NNN) and the app shows every job in that thread in order. For kind fill, the ask lists the [brackets] Kyle left in a scene (### B1, B2 ...) and the ## Result answers each under the same heading; the app puts the answers into the page and the agent never edits the scene.
